D005-D018_h023.question:
I’ve been off for maybe three months now. It started around the time I wrapped that war documentary, but I’m not sure if it’s because of that or just… something snapped. I keep having this overwhelming sense that everything’s winding down, like the world’s on the verge of collapsing. It’s not just anxiety; it feels certain, like I’m watching the last act and everyone else is oblivious.

Sometimes I just freeze. My ex came by to drop off our son last week and I was sitting on the couch, staring at the wall. I could hear them talking, but I couldn’t move or answer. It’s like my body just shuts down; I’m there, but not really there, and it can last for what feels like ages.

I also get these weird tastes in my mouth, like metal or something rotten, out of nowhere, even when I’m not eating. It’s strong enough that I have to spit or rinse my mouth, but nothing changes.

Ever since I filmed that explosion scene overseas—there were real casualties nearby—I haven’t quite felt back to normal, but I don’t know if this is about that or something different.
D005-D018_h023.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D018_h023.answer: C & B. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h024.question:
It’s hard to explain without sounding crazy, but something’s been off for about three months now.

Out in the woods, things feel like they’re aimed at me somehow. Like, I’ll hear the radio chatter from the other rangers, and it feels like they’re talking in code about me, even when they’re just giving weather updates. When hikers walk past and laugh, I catch myself thinking they’re laughing at me or testing me. I know it doesn’t quite make sense, but it still feels that way.

I also keep smelling smoke that isn’t there. Not the usual campfire smell—more like this sharp, chemical burn, or sometimes like something rotten. I’ll go checking the tree line, climbing the tower, looking for a fire, but there’s nothing. It’s gotten me pretty worked up a few times; I end up pacing around the cabin, can’t sit still, hands shaking, like I need to be doing something but don’t know what.

Losing my wife in that car wreck years back, and a bad incident on the job, they’re always in the back of my mind—but I can’t tell if this is from that or something different.
D005-D018_h024.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D018_h024.answer: C & B. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h025.question:
I’ve been driving buses for over twenty years, and I’ve always been pretty steady, but the last three months have been strange for me.

It started not long after that accident on my route—the one where the car ran the light and we barely stopped in time. Nobody died, but it shook me up. Since then, I feel like something’s “off.” At home, I’ve become fixated on the idea that my wife is seeing someone else. There’s nothing concrete—no texts, no late nights—but when she laughs at her phone or dresses up a bit, I’m convinced it’s for another man. I check her phone when she showers, watch how she talks to our neighbor. I know it sounds unreasonable, but it feels absolutely true in the moment.

I also keep getting these weird tastes in my mouth, out of nowhere—like metal, or something sweet and rotten—when I’m just sitting or driving. It doesn’t match anything I’ve eaten. And my wife says I’ve been moving strangely, like I do these little stiff, exaggerated turns to check the mirrors or open doors, almost like I’m acting it out instead of just doing it. I don’t mean to; it just happens.
D005-D018_h025.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D018_h025.answer: C & B. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
